critiques.rationale: A small set of computed headline figures would help an infographic communicate its story quickly before readers inspect the detailed ranking and trend views.

critiques.title: Show the final year on the trend axis
critiques.issue: The trend chart title says 1979–2023, but the x-axis labels stop at 2020, so the displayed endpoint is not explicitly marked.
critiques.rationale: When the story depends on long-term change through 2023, omitting the final labeled year creates avoidable ambiguity about the latest point.
critiques.evidence: The x-axis values list 1979, 1990, 2000, 2010, and 2020, while the data includes 2023 observations for all three birds.
critiques.suggestion: Add 2023 to the x-axis tick values so the chart's stated time span is fully visible.

critiques.title: Combine species and line-style meaning into one clearer legend
critiques.issue: The trend chart encodes species with both color and stroke pattern, but the separate color and strokeDash legends duplicate the same categories and make the meaning harder to parse.
critiques.rationale: A single combined legend would preserve the redundant cue needed for accessibility while reducing legend clutter and making the decline/non-decline distinction easier to read.
critiques.evidence: Both color and strokeDash are mapped to bird, and each has its own legend positioned at the top-right.
critiques.suggestion: Keep the stroke pattern encoding on the lines, but remove the duplicate strokeDash legend so one legend carries the species labels.

critiques.title: Give the long-term trend view the dominant position
critiques.issue: The largest tile is the ranking chart, even though the story's distinctive message comes from the population change view.
critiques.rationale: A narrative layout should give the most explanatory panel the strongest visual weight so the conservation message leads rather than the familiar ranking alone.
critiques.evidence: The ranking tile occupies the tallest, largest area on the left, while the trend tile that shows decline is smaller and compressed into the upper-right quadrant.
critiques.suggestion: Reflow the board so the trend chart becomes the hero panel, with the ranking and callout supporting it.

critiques.title: Use the same highlight color for House Sparrow across the ranking and callout
critiques.issue: The dashboard's strongest narrative species, House Sparrow, is highlighted in orange in the trend chart and callout but appears in the same muted green as every other bar in the ranking chart.
critiques.rationale: In an infographic, repeating one species cue across views helps readers connect the ranking, trend, and callout without re-decoding the story each time.
critiques.evidence: The ranking bars use a single green mark color, while House Sparrow is orange in the trend color scale and the did-you-know percentage callout is also orange.
critiques.suggestion: Color only the House Sparrow bar with the same orange used elsewhere and keep the remaining ranking bars neutral.

critiques.title: Anchor the trend chart to its stated 1979 baseline
critiques.issue: The trend chart says the index is normalized to 1979 = 100, but the y-scale starts at zero, which visually overstates the distance from the baseline and weakens the intended comparison to that reference point.
critiques.rationale: For a narrative chart about change from a fixed baseline, making the baseline itself visible supports more accurate reading of decline versus growth than a zero-based scale that is not the semantic reference.
critiques.evidence: The y-axis title defines the metric as 'Index (1979 = 100)', while the y scale is explicitly set to zero and no baseline rule at 100 is shown.
critiques.suggestion: Start the y-scale around the meaningful comparison range and draw a reference line at 100 so readers can judge which species are above or below their 1979 level.

critiques.title: Bring the bird selector into the comparison area
critiques.issue: The bird filter sits alone in a left rail while the two linked analytical views it controls begin well to the right, creating a disconnected control-to-content relationship.
critiques.rationale: Placing a control closer to the views it affects reduces scanning and makes the ranking-to-trend comparison feel like one coordinated story block.
critiques.evidence: The filter is placed in a left-rail panel, while the first chart starts at x=228 and both filter targets are the ranking and trend tiles.
critiques.suggestion: Reflow the board so the ranking and trend/callout cluster reads as one unit with the selector adjacent to the charts it filters, rather than isolated in a separate rail.

critiques.title: Document when illustrative values should be replaced with production data
critiques.issue: The dashboard mixes story-ready presentation with labels that say the data is illustrative, but there is no visible evidence of a publication rule for swapping in final sourced values.
critiques.rationale: For an editorial infographic, a lightweight handoff rule helps preserve trust and prevents a polished narrative from being published with placeholder or non-final numbers.
critiques.evidence: Both the ranking subtitle text and the source line in the callout explicitly say “illustrative.”
critiques.suggestion: Add a production checklist step that requires replacing illustrative labels with final sourced wording and verifying the headline takeaway against the final numbers before publication.
